_comment: One-action-steps pass, 22 Oct 2026 (QA lead: "Yes, fix all 113 cases"; and 22 Oct: no unnecessary steps). All six design-recheck cases were scanned; three have a step with two actions and are given here as full new field values (custom_steps and custom_expected). Only the steps and the "Step N:" result lines change; preconditions, title, quotes, From lines, build line, References from Design and the AUTOMATION line are byte-identical to the current bodies in design-recheck-2026-10-20/applied/. C690658, C690659 and C690663: every step is already one action (an action plus the reading of its own outcome, e.g. "Open {Work-order-2} and compare ..."); no unnecessary step; no change. Draft only: nothing written to TestRail.

690660.custom_steps:
1. Turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  2. Expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  3. Read {Part-sale-1}'s row in the Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin columns and compare it with the picture of board 4.10.
  4. Export the Expanded CSV and read the same row's Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin cells.
  5. Export the Expanded PDF and read the same cells.
690660.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: a Sales Type column shows.
  • Step 2: {Part-sale-1} shows as one row with Sales Type "Part Sales".
  • Step 3: each labor column shows a dash ("—"), as in the picture (today's report, board 4.3, shows 0.00 and $0.00 there).
  • Step 4: those cells are blank, as in the picture of board 4.11.
  • Step 5: those cells show a dash, as in the picture of board 4.12.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R9: “A part sale is one "Part Sales" row holding every dollar of the invoice.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”
  • S5-R15b: “On a Part Sales row, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin, and the labor and hours cells of the Expanded downloads, show a dash on screen and in the PDF and are blank in the CSV. A part sale has no labor, so these columns don't apply to it.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", row 46, read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 39: “39. (a) A dash on screen and in the PDF, and an empty cell in the CSV, as the design shows. A part sale has no labor, so the labor columns don't apply to it; it's the same rule as answers 24 and 25. This changes today's 0.00 / $0.00, so it's now listed under Release day. New S5-R15b, PRD v11.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.3 Before: expanded; 4.10 Expanded with Sales Type; 4.11 Expanded export (CSV); 4.12 Expanded export (PDF) (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: They agree now. On 21 Oct 2026 Chris Ward ruled for the design's dash and blank cells (answer 39, quoted above), and PRD version 11 added it as S5-R15b.

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-03-b-sbr-expanded.png, sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png, sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png, sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png.

  • Design — board 4.3 note: “Production today. One row per invoice under each rep.”
  • Design — board 4.10 title: “4.10 Expanded with Sales Type”
  • Design — board 4.10 note: “Values: Labor, Parts and Part Sales. One rep with both sides of one work order shows as one row reading "Labor, Parts" (S1-32, decision 38). S1-12: Devon "Parts" ($266.18), Elliot "Labor" ($2,186.82), shop supplies ($175.50) with Labor (decision 37).” “At 1600px wide, the columns after Parts Margin scroll under the pinned Subtotal; production behaves the same.”
  • Design — board 4.11 title: “4.11 Expanded export (CSV)”

690660.why: Step 1 bundled two actions (turn the Sales Type column on, expand {Sales-rep-A}); split into two steps. The old Step 1 result moves to the new Step 2 (the expand shows the row); the new Step 1 gets a neutral result. Old steps 2-4 become 3-5 with their results unchanged.

690664.custom_steps:
1. Expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  2. Expand {Sales-rep-B}.
  3. Read the Adjustments column on {Work-order-1}'s Labor row and on its Parts row.
  4. Export the Expanded CSV and read the Adjustments cells of the same two rows.
  5. Export the Expanded PDF and read the Adjustments cells of the same two rows.
690664.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Sales-rep-A}'s invoice rows show.
  • Step 2: {Work-order-1}'s invoice shows one Labor row under {Sales-rep-A} and one Parts row under {Sales-rep-B}.
  • Step 3: Adjustments reads ($30.00) on the Labor row and ($20.00) on the Parts row (600 ÷ 1,000 × 50 and 400 ÷ 1,000 × 50): each row shows only its own share; the $30.00 shop supplies sit on the Labor row.
  • Step 4: the CSV shows the same two shares under Adjustments: the $30.00 discount share on the Labor row and the $20.00 share on the Parts row.
  • Step 5: the PDF shows the same two shares under Adjustments.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R6: “Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared between the Labor and the Parts rows in proportion to each side's labor or parts dollars after that side's line fees and discounts, measured by size whatever their sign. The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00. Each row shows its share in its Adjustments column.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”

From: Chris Ward's answers, question sheet of 19 Oct 2026, Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", rows 6-43 (answered 19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 22: “22. (a) as the feature spec. Yes, the Sales By Representative definition changes to the row's share.”
